prompt: Write a note to a friend about a funny thing that happened with a neighbor. Aim for about 400 words. Reply with the note only.
final_message:
Dear friend,

I have a small story for you, and I'm still laughing about it, so you must forgive me if it comes out crooked.

Last Tuesday morning I opened the door and found a peach pie sitting on my porch step, still faintly warm, with a clean cloth tucked over the top. There was no note, and I looked up and down the road and saw nobody. I decided right then that some kind soul had remembered I'd been under the weather, and I carried it in like a prize.

I cut a slice for my breakfast, which I admit is not how a sensible woman starts her day. By noon I had cut another, and by supper I had told myself that a pie that size could not possibly keep, and that it would be a sin to let good peaches go to waste. By evening there was about half of it left, and I felt rather well looked after.

Then Mrs. Dunning from the next farm over came walking up the lane with her hat pulled low and a very careful look on her face. She stood on my step for a good while talking about the weather and her hens and her sister's knee. At last she said she had set a pie down by mistake at the wrong gate, and that it had been meant for the new preacher, who was coming to supper at her place that very night.

I said nothing for a moment, because there was nothing sensible to say. Then I told her the pie had been very good, and that I was sorry to report the preacher would be getting a smaller share than she planned.

She looked at me, and I looked at her, and then she began to laugh so hard she had to hold on to my porch rail. I have never seen a woman so red in the face. She said she had walked a mile and a half rehearsing how to ask, and had worried the whole way that I'd be offended.

Of course I wasn't. I gave her the rest of the pie on my best plate, and she went home and cut it so the missing part didn't show, and told the preacher it was a family way of serving. I hear he had two helpings and asked for the recipe.

I plan to bake her one on Saturday, a whole pie, and I intend to put my name on it.

Write soon and tell me what your neighbors are up to, for I'm sure it can't be as good as mine.

Hattie
